name: Public-evidence satellite maneuver benchmark
notes: Event labels are interval-censored public operator evidence. Verified-quiet controls require an authoritative statement that the spacecraft could not or would not execute commanded orbital maneuvers during the selected interval. Unknown windows are excluded from false-positive denominators.
data_attribution: Basic SSA orbital data from Space-Track.org, operated by U.S. Space Command. Public maneuver evidence is cited per case.
split_policy: All windows for a NORAD object belong to exactly one satellite-level split. The primary test split contains objects never used for calibration.

cases.description: Sentinel-1A collision-avoidance maneuver during LEOP. ESA reports a 39-second maneuver executed at 05:14 UTC on 5 April 2014.
Negative control. NASA reports ACRIMSAT went silent in December 2013; ESA reports it had run out of fuel and could no longer be maneuvered by April 2014.
NASA and SpaceX Dragon reboost demonstration.
ISS reboost using Progress 83P thrusters. NASA gives the date and duration but not a precise UTC start time.
Negative control after Meteosat-7 disposal. EUMETSAT reports the fuel tank was empty and instruments switched off after the final graveyard-orbit burns.
ESA reports 11 recovery maneuvers over 17 days; individual burn times are not public in the cited source.
Negative control after GIOVE-A decommissioning. ESA reports the onboard computer and transmitter were switched off and the attitude/orbit-control system put in standby.
First INTEGRAL disposal-orbit burn, reported by ESA as occurring on 12-13 January 2015.
Negative control after the January 2024 disposal maneuver sequence. ESA states the January maneuvers set the trajectory so the orbit would evolve to the targeted September reentry.
Unlabelled control retained for robustness analysis only. It is excluded from false-positive denominators.
cases.source: Public-evidence review required before any negative label is assigned.
